messages:
nayan: flipping the min-TLS enforcement canary in eu-west at 02:10 UTC to require >= TLS1.3. seeing a flurry of interservice handshake failures immediately after. rolling back? :grimacing:
beth: logs show a subset of internal proxies returning 'unsupported protocol' during ClientHello. different behavior across regions. looks like some legacy sidecars haven't received the new CA bundle that includes the cross-signing cert
omar: paste a sample from service mesh logs? curious if it's TLS version negotiation or cert validation failing
nayan: mesh logs (redacted):
```
mesh-proxy[sidecar-72]: 2026-03-24T02:11:18Z warn: tls: unsupported protocol client=svc-account:worker-eu server=svc-account:router-eu
router[router-9]: 2026-03-24T02:11:18Z error: handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority client=svc-account:worker-eu
keystore[rotator]: 2026-03-24T02:11:18Z info: signed cert issued key=projects/redwood/keys/serving-cert-v3 principal=svc-account:router-eu key_version=2
keystore[rotator]: 2026-03-24T02:11:19Z error: unwrap failed key=projects/redwood/keys/serving-cert-v3 err=403 KMSDecryptDenied principal=svc-account:worker-eu
```
beth: interesting — two different failure modes: 1) unsupported protocol (clients trying TLS1.2?) 2) KMS unwrap denies for cert retrieval during handshake. Could be simultaneous rollout of TLS min enforcement and a KMS policy change or alias promotion
lina: timeline from audit-trail: 2026-03-24T01:45 UTC change-set: 1) infra pushed a KMS alias swap for serving-cert-v3 -> serving-cert-v3b 2) security enabled feature flag to enforce TLS>=1.3 in the router canary 3) an RBAC role-binding for service-account:worker-eu to access keystore-v3 was scheduled but not applied in eu-west canary due to a merge drift. So some proxies requested certs under the new alias without permissions
omar: so race: some proxies enforce TLS1.3 (which triggers cert re-fetch with new SNI/policy?) and keystore alias rotation + missing RBAC means some unwraps get 403. Others fall back with TLS1.2 which our router rejects. double-whammy causing varied errors
oncall: applying hotfix: revert TLS min enforcement flag in eu-west canary (kubectl patch configmap/proxy-flags -n mesh --type merge -p '{"data":{"min_tls":"1.2"}}') and re-enable rotator cache TTL=45s to reduce unwrap frequency
sec-bot: alert: interservice-handshake-failures exceeded baseline in eu-west at 2026-03-24T02:14:02Z. incident INC-185100 opened
beth: also patching RBAC to bind service-account:worker-eu to role keystore-decrypt-temp in keystore namespace while infra reconciles alias mappings
ayan: running the RBAC patch now: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: keystore-decrypt-temp-worker-eu
  namespace: keystore
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: worker-eu
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: keystore-decrypt-temporary
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF
```
lina: good. follow-ups: 1) make alias rotation plan require a preflight canary that verifies RBAC and unwraps from each region 2) gate TLS min enforcement on successful unwrap smoke tests 3) add a deploy checklist entry: "ensure rotator cache is present during alias switchover" 4) expand decision-level audit logs to include effective policy reason (why deny was returned)
omar: also add a mesh upgrade job that verifies protocol negotiation across a matrix of client versions (TLS1.2/1.3) so we don't assume all sidecars are identical
oncall: monitoring shows handshake error rate back to baseline ~5m after patches. keeping the temporary RBAC for 1h and leaving rotator cache at 45s until alias is confirmed consistent
beth: created SEC-2026-121 to track follow-ups and owners: infra (alias orchestration), mesh (canary gating), sec (audit-level enhancement)
ayan: we'll do a short blameless postmortem with exact audit ids and timeline. also adding a runbook step: "if TLS enforcement causes errors, check keystore alias and RBAC before deciding to rollback"
lina: adding a small integration test to CI that runs during alias swaps: spawn 50 concurrent handshake flows across regions and verify unwrap success and protocol negotiation. low-risk but catches this class of race
ayan: thanks all — big win on ops speed. leaving notes for oncall to follow for next 24h :heart:
